met_analysis:
The Low Pressure Area (Remnant of Very Severe Cyclonic Storm “Arnab”) overnorth Chhattisgarh & adjoining East Madhya Pradesh, southeast Uttar Pradesh and west Jharkhand lies over southeast Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood at 0530 hrs IST of 31st October, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
Yesterday's Low Pressure Area over South Andaman Sea & adjoining North Andaman Sea and Andaman & Nicobar Islands moved west-northwestwards and lay as a Well Marked Low pressure area over southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Andaman Sea at 0530 hrs IST of today, the 31st October 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and concentrate into a Depression over the same region during next 12 hours. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move west-northwestwards and reach over westcentral Bay of Bengal near Andhra Pradesh coast around evening of 2nd November 2026.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Haryana & neighbourhood at 4.5 km above mean sea level persists with the trough aloft in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 78°E to the north of Lat. 27°N.
The trough now runs from eastcentral Arabian Sea off Maharashtra coast to cyclonic circulation associated with the Low Pressure area over southeast Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood across Konkan & Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Vidarbha and Madhya Pradesh at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over North Interior Karnataka & neighbourhood and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over South Gujarat & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Assam & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The trough from northwest Uttar Pradesh to the cyclonic circulation associated with the Low Pressure Area over north Chhattisgarh & adjoining East Madhya Pradesh, southeast Uttar Pradesh and west Jharkhand at 3.1 km above mean sea levelhas become less marked.
